protocol.name: enzui_material_v1

description.summary: liquid glass over what lies behind a surface

protocol.description:
A client asks the compositor to paint enzUI's sampled-backdrop material (liquid glass) in parts of a surface. The compositor samples whatever it has drawn below the surface (the wallpaper, other windows, panels), blurs, refracts, tints and contrast-protects it exactly as enzUI-ICED does inside an application, and then draws the surface's own content on top. The surface itself should be transparent where its glass is.
The material is the framework's: each region carries the same tokens `enzui_theme::MaterialTokens` holds, so a theme or a style change is the client's to make and the compositor never guesses an appearance.

request.name: get_surface_material

description.summary: the material object of one surface

request.description: At most one per wl_surface at a time.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a material object

request.name: destroy
request.description: The regions are removed on the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_regions
request.description:
Double-buffered: applied on the next wl_surface.commit. An empty array removes every region.
Each region is 25 little-endian 32-bit floats: 0-3 x, y, width, height of its rounded rectangle, in surface-local logical pixels; 4 corner radius, logical pixels; 5-20 the material tokens in MaterialTokens order: blur_sigma, refraction, bevel_width, index_of_refraction, dispersion, color_diffusion, color_reach, optical_depth, tint_opacity, saturation, highlight, brightness, light_angle (degrees), profile_curvature, contrast_protection, protected_inset; 21-24 the tint colour, sRGB-encoded red, green, blue, and alpha.
At most 32 regions. A non-finite value, a negative size or more regions than allowed is a protocol error.

request.name: set_shadow

description.summary: a soft shadow outside every region

request.description: Double-buffered like set_regions. The compositor draws it around the glass, after sampling the backdrop, so the glass never sees its own shadow. A surface cannot draw this itself: its own shadow would lie under the transparent glass too. Zero opacity removes it.

arg.name: opacity
arg.summary: black at this opacity next to the edge, 0 to 1

request.name: set_measure_only

description.summary: measure the backdrop without painting glass

request.description: Double-buffered like set_regions. While nonzero, the compositor measures the backdrop behind every region (see the luminance event) but paints neither the glass nor its shadow: a surface whose ink follows its backdrop learns its ink before its glass appears.

event.name: luminance

description.summary: the backdrop's brightness behind a region

event.description: The average brightness of what lies behind region `region` (its index in the last set_regions), from 0 to 1 in perceptual (sRGB-encoded) terms, measured as the framework's renderer measures it: over the inner 80% of the filtered backdrop, clear of the rim. Sent when a region is first measured and whenever the value moves by 1/128 or more; it describes a frame or two ago.

request.name: set_cutouts

description.summary: where the surface covers its glass

request.description:
Double-buffered like set_regions. Rounded rectangles where the surface draws opaque content over its glass, such as the panes of a window whose frame is glass: the compositor neither filters the backdrop for, nor paints, the glass inside them, so glass behind opaque content costs nothing. The corners outside a cutout's radius still show glass.
Each cutout is 5 little-endian 32-bit floats: x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels, and the corner radius. At most 32; an empty array removes them. A non-finite value or a negative size is a protocol error.

entry.name: invalid_regions
entry.summary: the array is not a whole number of valid regions

entry.name: invalid_cutouts
entry.summary: the array is not a whole number of valid cutouts
